full_judgment: 3. The defendants contested the suit denying the plaintiffs claim, inter-alia, that according to them Haji Kala Miah took settlement of the suit land by patta dated 22.02.1894 from Nazamuddin Howlader. Kala Miah died leaving two wives, Hasan Banu and Hazera Banu, one son `farm Miah and two daughters named Syedun Nessa and Khosh Meher. Hasan I3anu died leaving son Tanu Miah and daughter, Syedun Nessa. Hazra .C3anu died leaving mother Ayesha Khatun, daughter Khosh Meher brother Besha Gazi Khosh Meher died leaving Ayesha Khatun and Syedun Nessa Besha Gazi gifted his entire sharer to his grand daughter Nurjahan. Syedun Nessa and Hasan Banu transferred .08 acres of land to these defendants and thereafter, she had only .02 acres of land which land she had gifted to Sufia Khatun. Tanu Miah was the owner on 2.08 acres of land but he got his name recorded in respect of the entire lands depriving the other co-sharers. Despite such recording, Tanu Miah's mother and sisters were in possession of their respective sharers farm Miah mortgaged the lands to Abdul Huq Bepari, who obtained decree in Title Suit No. 113 of 1931 against Tanu Miah. Though Abdul Huq Bepari purchased the lands but he could not get possession through Court. Abdul Huq Bepari transferred 0.91 acres of land to defendants. He also transferred .75 acres of land to Safia Khatun. After such transfer, Tanu Miah had only .034 acres 'of land. Sabiha"Khatun acquired 2.06 acres of land by way of purchase and inheritance and thereafter, she transferred .03 acres of land to the plaintiff and his brother Rafiqullah. On the death of Rafiqullah the plaintiff did not inherit his share inasmuch as Rafiqullah had mother Angura Khatun and sisters Atorennessa and Monowara Khatun who were not made parties-in the suit.
